issue.title: KAFKA-21034: Wipe the global state directory when the store is corrupted

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
GlobalStreamThread#initialize already wipes the global state directory when
stateConsumer.initialize() throws InvalidOffsetException, but a corrupted state store is not
handled the same way.

When the RocksDB invalid-state check fails under EOS, RocksDBStore#openDB wraps the resulting
ProcessorStateException in a TaskCorruptedException. TaskCorruptedException is a sibling of
ProcessorStateException rather than a subclass. It therefore falls through to the generic
catch (StreamsException) in GlobalStreamThread#initialize, which calls
closeStateConsumer(stateConsumer, false), and the corrupted directory is left on disk. Every
restart hits the same state, which becomes a crash loop under an automatic restart policy such
as a Kubernetes StatefulSet.

This extends the existing InvalidOffsetException handler to also catch TaskCorruptedException,
closing the state consumer with wipeStateStore=true so the next start rebuilds the global
store from the changelog. GlobalStateUpdateTask#close already logs "Deleting global task
directory after detecting corruption" on that path, so the deletion itself was already
implemented, but it was never reached for this exception.

This PR also fixes a double-cleanup bug affecting the existing InvalidOffsetException path.
When a global store was already registered, the inner catch closed the stores, but the outer
catch attempted to flush them again. This could throw IllegalStateException before
startupException was assigned, causing start() to return without throwing and leaving the
thread state at CREATED. Clearing the local stateConsumer reference after cleanup prevents the
outer catch from closing it again.

The existing shouldDieOnInvalidOffsetExceptionDuringStartup test is updated to trigger the
exception during initialization: previously, equal beginning and end offsets caused it to skip
restoration polling and exercise the running-thread path instead. It now verifies that start()
throws with the expected cause and the thread reaches DEAD. Two new tests cover
TaskCorruptedException during startup, and the same case with another global store already
registered.

**Does this need a KIP?**
I do not think so, but I would like this confirmed. The wipe on the InvalidOffsetException
path was introduced in KAFKA-10306 (2020) and the wipeStateStore flag in KAFKA-8897 (2021),
both without a KIP. This change routes TaskCorruptedException through the existing
state-cleanup path. The double-cleanup fix ensures that initialization failures are propagated
by start() on both exception paths. These are bug fixes and introduce no new configuration or
public API. If that reasoning is wrong, please let me know and I will open a KIP instead.

**Verification**
- ./gradlew streams:test --tests GlobalStreamThreadTest: 19 tests, 0 failures
- ./gradlew streams:checkstyleTest streams:spotlessCheck: passed
- Re-verified after merging trunk to resolve the conflict with #23407.
- Removing TaskCorruptedException from the extended catch makes both corruption tests fail:
  the exception propagates unwrapped, so getCause() returns null instead of the expected
  TaskCorruptedException.
- Removing the stateConsumer reset makes the already-registered-store test and the existing
  shouldDieOnInvalidOffsetExceptionDuringStartup fail, because start() returns without
  throwing.

Reviewers: Uladzislau Blok <blokv75@gmail.com>
